name: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
scope_notes: International public-health research, systematic reviews and policy analysis; local findings need international significance. For primary research, at least one author must have an institutional affiliation in the country where the research took place. Systematic reviews require multilingual searches performed within six months of submission; guidance also calls for protocol registration. The journal normally excludes work published elsewhere, with a preprint exception specifically for research in a public-health emergency of international concern. These conditions materially limit independent-author and ordinary preprinted-work fit.

route.conditions: WHO charges no author fees. Research, systematic reviews and policy/practice articles normally have 3000-word limits; there is no paid excess-length route stated. Abstract translation is free. Supplementary material for accepted work must be placed in a DOI-issuing repository; use a free suitable repository. Authors obtain permissions for copyrighted reuse. Apply current affiliation, review-search recency and preprint restrictions.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None for the stated journal route. DOI-repository choice and any third-party reuse permissions can create external costs; free suitable alternatives are needed.

fee_evidence.note: Sections 1.1 and 2.5 exclude all author fees; section 2.3 makes abstract translation free. Article limits and DOI-repository requirements are stated on the same full page.

difficulty.basis: Initial editorial screening requires originality, scientific rigour and explicit new knowledge, but no acceptance statistic or comparative contribution threshold was found. These requirements alone do not establish a relative difficulty band. International relevance and country-affiliation rules are fit conditions, not a prestige score.

metrics.name: Journal Impact Factor
metrics.population: Journal-level citation metric; underlying citable-item count is not disclosed on the WHO page.
metrics.note: Officially labelled 2025. Citation impact is separate from acceptance difficulty.

audit_note: Independent skeptical review read the full current official contributor policy at https://www.who.int/publications/journals/bulletin/contributors/guidelines-for-contributors and About page. Fee audit and unknown difficulty retained. Scope replacement makes the primary-research affiliation and narrow preprint exception explicit, rather than implying generic preprint acceptance. The country-affiliation rule does not automatically apply to every secondary analysis; the policy names primary research. This is a journal-policy check, not an ethics determination.

name: Revista Panamericana de Salud Pública / Pan American Journal of Public Health
scope_notes: Public health in the Americas, including population analyses, methodology, health systems and systematic reviews. Relevance beyond the study locality and across the region matters; noncritical descriptive literature reviews and clinical case reports are normally excluded.

route.conditions: Diamond open access without author/researcher charges or selective fee waiver. English, Portuguese and Spanish manuscripts are accepted. Follow article-specific length and table/reference limits in the full author instructions; no paid excess-page option is stated. Authors obtain permissions for copyrighted reuse and meet data-availability requirements. Regional public-health relevance remains essential.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None stated under the blanket no-researcher-fees policy; no compulsory membership, page charge or editing purchase was found in the full guidance.

fee_evidence.note: Full official page read with urllib despite browser 403: publication costs authors nothing and the diamond model has no fees for researchers or readers.

Complete current official instructions read with urllib: identifies a free open-access journal, specifies manuscript limits and permissions duties, and states no compulsory author payment or membership.

difficulty.basis: Editors assess methodological soundness, novelty and applicability after scope screening, but these criteria do not establish a comparative difficulty band. No dated official acceptance statistics were found. Relevance to public health in the Americas is a fit requirement.

audit_note: Access: page for both official pages, retrieved in full with Python urllib after the web tool returned HTTP 403. At least three reviewers are described, but reviewer count is not acceptance selectivity. No metric copied from a third-party journal directory.

name: Emerging Infectious Diseases
publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
scope_notes: Epidemiology and prevention of emerging or reemerging infectious diseases worldwide. OSRI fit includes existing surveillance-data analyses, modeling and syntheses with an explicit public health contribution; laboratory and clinical portions of journal scope are outside this catalog intended initial research use.

route.conditions: No author fees for ordinary articles, including submission, pages and corrections. Article-specific limits are enforced; research and synopsis articles normally allow 3500 text words. No required society membership or registration is stated for ordinary research/synopsis articles. Supplement organizers incur separate costs; this route does not cover organizing a supplement.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None for standard individual-article submission/publication. Supplement-organizer costs are excluded.

fee_evidence.note: Current official page updated 8 October 2026 expressly excludes submission fees, page charges, correction costs and other author fees; the supplement section separates organizer costs from author fees.
Official submission instructions explicitly exclude submitting and processing fees and enforce article word limits.
The official 2024 report independently excludes submission, page, correction and other author fees; dated corroboration.

Current article table updated 15 September 2026 specifies length limits; ordinary research and synopsis categories have no membership prerequisite. The network-letter category has a separate network-affiliation condition.

difficulty.basis: Provisional agent judgment: official sources describe acceptance of approximately one quarter of submitted articles. The current general-information page reports 23.7%, whereas the 2024 report and EID Advantage describe about 25%; none specifies a comparable acceptance cohort. Emerging-infection/public-health relevance remains a separate fit condition.

metrics.name: Reported acceptance proportion, undated current summary
metrics.population: Submitted articles, not only externally reviewed articles; exact count, cohort dates and treatment of invited manuscripts are not supplied.
metrics.note: Page updated 24 September 2026; this is the page date, not a stated acceptance-statistic year. Not an individual manuscript probability.

metrics.name: Typical annual acceptance proportion reported in 2024 journal report
metrics.population: All submissions in an unspecified typical annual period; approximately 2000 manuscripts per year is contextual volume, not an exact denominator.
metrics.note: The report is titled 2024 but does not identify the proportion as a measured 2024 cohort. Preserved separately from the current 23.7% summary.

metrics.name: CiteScore
metrics.population: Journal-level Scopus citation metric; underlying document count is not disclosed on the CDC page.
metrics.note: Official source explicitly labels this 2025. Citation impact is not used to infer acceptance difficulty.

audit_note: Access: page for CDC General Information, EID Advantage and the complete 2024 report PDF. Acceptance summaries have different precision and unspecified periods; no false reconciliation. The 2025 report PDF was located and its bytes retrieved, but the web tool rejected full text extraction because of file size; its indexed introduction supplied no acceptance statistic, so no metric is attributed to that unread report. CDC impact-factor pages mix report-year labels with undated current summaries; those values were not normalized into an assumed citation year.

name: Eurosurveillance
publisher: European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control
scope_notes: Communicable-disease epidemiology, surveillance, prevention and control with European relevance, including relevant work conducted outside Europe. ECDC expressly lists regular research, surveillance and outbreak articles, reviews, rapid communications and perspectives. Existing surveillance-data analyses and syntheses can fit. Exact current article-length and submission requirements still need journal-author-guidance confirmation because that page returned HTTP 403.

route.conditions: Ordinary journal articles use a diamond route free to authors and readers under ECDC funding. No waiver, institutional payment agreement or paid membership is needed for this stated route. The journal author pages remain blocked; check current article-type length and submission requirements before preparing a manuscript. This record does not establish supplement-organizer terms.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None for the ordinary author route under the publisher blanket free-to-authors statement; special supplement-organizer terms not audited.

fee_evidence.note: Current full publisher page identifies the Eurosurveillance Editorial Office and describes its journal specifically as diamond open access free of charge to readers and authors.
Official 2025 publisher notice says all Eurosurveillance content is open access free to readers and authors, with ECDC procuring editorial/copyediting support.
Current journal-specific author page still returns 403; precise article-length guidance was not directly inspected.

difficulty.basis: Provisional agent judgment: the editorial team's 2025 retrospective reports one in five articles accepted and 1050 submissions. The count and acceptance summary are journal-wide, not a forecast for an OSRI paper. European relevance is a scope condition; the editorial explicitly includes relevant work from outside Europe.

metrics.name: Reported acceptance proportion
metrics.population: Articles submitted to the journal; the same retrospective reports 1050 submissions, but does not define a finalized submission cohort or accepted-count numerator.
metrics.note: Primary editorial by the Eurosurveillance editorial team, discussing 2025. Do not manufacture an exact 210 accepted count or infer manuscript odds.

metrics.name: Manuscript submissions received
metrics.population: All journal submissions received in 2025; the separately reported 149 pre-submission enquiries are not added.
metrics.note: Journal-wide volume, not the externally reviewed subset.

audit_note: Independent review retrieved both current journal-specific ECDC publisher pages cited by the fee auditor. The organisational page explicitly identifies a diamond journal free to authors/readers; the 2025 editing-services notice confirms the article taxonomy and independent peer review. Retain verified_free for ordinary articles and replace historical review evidence with this stronger publisher source. The 2025 retrospective independently confirms 1050 submissions and one in five accepted; it does not establish a finalized submission cohort or exact accepted numerator. Author guidance remains blocked; no length limit was invented.

name: Journal of Public Health
publisher: Oxford University Press for the Faculty of Public Health
scope_notes: Broad public health research, health improvement/protection, healthcare public health, ethics and law, with translation into practice. Secondary-data papers fit the broad original-work remit; reporting guidance addresses systematic reviews, although a dedicated review format is not separately listed.

route.conditions: The standard non-OA licence has no licence charge, and the journal explicitly has no page or colour charges. Optional open access requires an APC or eligible institutional funding. Original papers normally have 2000–3000 words and up to four tables/figures. A submission fee was neither stated nor explicitly excluded in the inspected guidance; confirm that cost before treating the complete route as free.
route.other_mandatory_costs: No page or colour charges and no mandatory membership stated. Submission fee remains unknown; optional OA is paid unless covered.

fee_evidence.note: Full current journal policy expressly excludes standard-licence, page and colour charges and distinguishes paid optional OA; its submission section does not establish no submission fee.
Journal-specific publisher page was inspected for a general free-author/submission policy; none was found.
Linked submission-system page returned 403, preventing additional fee confirmation.

difficulty.basis: Official grading emphasizes scientific originality, impact and relevance to public-health practice. No quantified acceptance selectivity or sufficiently discriminating contribution threshold was found to establish a comparative band. The published decision medians include desk rejections and do not imply easy acceptance.

metrics.name: Journal Impact Factor
metrics.population: Journal-level citation metric; underlying citable-item count not reported in the journal table.
metrics.note: Official 2025 label; not an acceptance metric.

metrics.name: CiteScore
metrics.population: Journal-level Scopus citation metric; underlying document count not reported in the journal table.
metrics.note: Official 2025 label; not an acceptance metric.

metrics.name: Median days from submission to first decision
metrics.population: Manuscripts with a first decision in 2025, including rejection without external review; n not reported.
metrics.note: Population definition: https://academic.oup.com/pages/using-the-content/metrics . Not peer-review duration for accepted papers.

metrics.name: Median days from submission to final decision
metrics.population: Manuscripts with a final accept/reject decision in 2025, including desk rejections; n not reported.
metrics.note: Population definition: https://academic.oup.com/pages/using-the-content/metrics .

metrics.name: Median days from acceptance to publication
metrics.population: Articles first published online in 2025; n not reported.
metrics.note: Population definition: https://academic.oup.com/pages/using-the-content/metrics . Post-acceptance production time.

audit_note: Access: page for official author guidelines, About table and OUP metric definitions. Fast overall decisions are not evidence of high acceptance. No route or fee fields changed.

name: Scandinavian Journal of Public Health
scope_notes: Public health original research, literature reviews and study-design papers. Existing-data population research and synthesis are relevant. The free route can substantially constrain review length because the printed-page threshold includes references, tables and figures.

route.conditions: Select standard subscription publication and keep original, review or design articles within five printed pages, counting abstract, tables, figures and references. Above five pages the mandatory charge is GBP 80 or USD 100 per excess page excluding VAT. Word limits alone do not establish free eligibility: reviews may allow 6000 words yet exceed five printed pages. Optional OA and requested print colour cost extra. Sponsored supplements are excluded.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None within the five-printed-page route without optional print colour/OA. Mandatory excess-page charges apply beyond five pages; supplement authors/sponsors fund supplement costs.

fee_evidence.note: Complete current journal instructions state no submission/publication fees, then impose GBP 80/USD 100 per printed page above five for original/review/design articles, excluding VAT; optional OA, requested print colour and supplements have separate costs.

difficulty.basis: Official guidelines describe scientific/editorial screening and external review, but provide no dated acceptance cohort or comparative selectivity threshold. General quality requirements do not justify a moderate/easy label. Nordic association and topic fit do not determine difficulty.

audit_note: Access: page for the full official author guidelines. The stated average 30-day decision has no measurement period, sample size or desk-rejection definition; it was not promoted into a dated performance metric. Access: blocked for attempted Sage metrics endpoints, including https://journals.sagepub.com/overview-metric/SJP (urllib HTTP 403).

name: Public Health Reports
publisher: Sage for the Association of Schools and Programs of Public Health
scope_notes: Public-health practice, epidemiologic research, evaluation, methodology, meta-analysis and topical synthesis with practical implications. The methodology category asks for applications and examples using original data; a purely conceptual method description is not an established fit. For work involving human participants or human data, guidance requires an institutional IRB, nonresearch or exemption basis; authors should not independently declare themselves exempt. Original research, methodology and topical reviews are peer reviewed; some other categories are editor assessed or need prior agreement. Recent data, preferably under five years old, are favored.

route.conditions: Standard subscription publication is free to submit and publish. Online colour is free; requested print colour and optional OA incur separate charges. Follow article-specific limits rather than assuming a paid excess-length option: the hosted instructions normally set 3000 words for original research and methodology. Some brief reports/commentaries require prior editorial agreement. No mandatory society membership is stated.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None for standard publication without optional print colour or OA. Third-party material permissions are the authors responsibility.

fee_evidence.note: Current official indexed policy explicitly excludes submitting and publishing fees and distinguishes optional print-colour/OA costs. Direct page fetch timed out; indexed content was available.

Directly read official hosted 32-page instructions, captured 25 June 2025: pages 1–3 exclude submission/publication charges, make online colour free and distinguish optional print colour and OA. Article limits are also specified.

difficulty.basis: Provisional agent judgment based on historical selectivity: the editors report 15.2% acceptance among 656 final decisions in 2023. This is a mixed peer/editor-reviewed regular-issue population, not current research-article odds. No 2024/2025 acceptance report was found in the bounded search; US public-health relevance is a separate fit condition.

metrics.name: Acceptance rate by final decisions
metrics.population: 100 acceptances among 656 final decisions on bimonthly peer/editor-reviewed content; excludes supplements and unreviewed content; includes letters and editor-reviewed departments.
metrics.note: Historical decision-year population, not 100 divided by new submissions.

metrics.name: New submissions received
metrics.population: 614 regular-issue submissions plus 20 invited/sponsored supplement submissions.
metrics.note: Different population from acceptance-rate denominator.

metrics.name: Median days to first decision
metrics.population: 617 first decisions in 2023 on bimonthly peer-reviewed content, including decisions on earlier submissions.
metrics.note: Interquartile range 7–25 days.

metrics.name: Median days from original submission to final acceptance
metrics.population: 116 peer/editor-reviewed articles published in volume 138, January–December 2023; excludes unreviewed special material.
metrics.note: Interquartile range 193–289 days; accepted/published articles only.

metrics.name: Median days from final acceptance to online publication
metrics.population: 123 full-content articles in volume 138, excluding reviewer acknowledgments and corrigenda.
metrics.note: Interquartile range 39–60 days; publication cohort differs from decision cohort.

audit_note: Independent review read the official 32-page hosted instructions captured 25 June 2025 at https://www.sagepub.com/docs/default-source/msg/submission-guidelines_-public-health-reports_-sage-journals.pdf and independently retrieved the current official indexed HTML fee and ethics text at https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/phr ; direct HTML timed out. The scope replacement exposes consequential methodology and institutional-ethics conditions for OSRI's existing-data work. The fee route is retained. Independently retrieved the full editors' 2023 report at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11284977/ and confirmed that the 15.2% rate uses 656 final decisions, with mixed peer/editor-reviewed content; it is historical and not research-article-specific.

name: Perspectives in Public Health
publisher: Sage for the Royal Society for Public Health
scope_notes: Applied public health and health promotion research, reviews and short reports. Secondary-data research and review methods can fit. Original research and reviews are subject to peer review; Current Topics and Opinions, In Practice and Features are editorial categories rather than equivalent peer-reviewed research.

route.conditions: Standard subscription route has no submission or publication fees. Online colour is free; requested print colour and optional OA cost extra. Original research/reviews normally require 2000–4000 words including abstracts, excluding references/tables/figures; no paid excess-length option is stated. A plain-language summary is required for article types needing an abstract. Optional professional author services are not required.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None for standard publication without optional print colour or OA; no compulsory society membership stated.

fee_evidence.note: Full current journal policy explicitly excludes submission/publication fees and distinguishes optional print-colour/OA costs; article and plain-language-summary requirements are stated on the same page.

difficulty.basis: Official quality screening and preference for research fitting upcoming themed issues are documented, but no dated acceptance statistics or comparative selectivity threshold were found. Issue-theme suitability is fit, not a prestige measure.

audit_note: Access: page for full official guidance. Original research/reviews/short reports use peer review; Current Topics and Opinions is editor assessed, so its ease cannot stand in for research-paper difficulty. Access: blocked for attempted Sage metric endpoints, including https://journals.sagepub.com/overview-metric/RSH (urllib HTTP 403).

name: European Journal of Public Health
publisher: Oxford University Press for the European Public Health Association
scope_notes: Multidisciplinary population health, epidemiology, health services and policy, with European focus and relevant global health contributions. Original articles expressly include systematic reviews and meta-analyses. Retained as an important conditional-cost counterexample, not an unconditional free recommendation.

route.conditions: Fully open access with compulsory APC: the inspected policy lists EUR 2956 regular charge and EUR 1408 for short reports. An eligible institutional agreement may pay it; qualifying full waivers are conditional and discretionary waivers are limited. EUPHA membership offers a 20% APC discount, not automatic free publication. No page/colour charges. Submission-fee absence is not explicit. Recheck price and route eligibility before submission.
route.other_mandatory_costs: Publication APC unless qualifying full coverage/waiver applies. No page or colour charges; membership optional. Submission fee unknown.

fee_evidence.note: Full current journal policy identifies fully OA publication, compulsory APCs, EUR 2956 regular/EUR 1408 short-report charges, conditional institutional coverage/waivers, 20% member discount and no page/colour fees; no explicit no-submission-fee statement.

difficulty.basis: Current author guidance describes peer review and international public-health fit. An editors' 2020 commentary mentions about 20% acceptance without a period or denominator; that historical statement is insufficient for a current comparative band. Citation scores and decision speed do not establish acceptance difficulty.

metrics.name: Journal Impact Factor
metrics.population: Journal-level citation metric; underlying citable-item count not reported in journal table.
metrics.note: Official 2025 label; not acceptance selectivity.

metrics.name: CiteScore
metrics.population: Journal-level Scopus citation metric; underlying document count not reported in journal table.
metrics.note: Official 2025 label; not acceptance selectivity.

metrics.name: Median days from submission to first decision
metrics.population: Manuscripts with a first decision in 2025, including rejection without external review; n not reported.
metrics.note: Population definition: https://academic.oup.com/pages/using-the-content/metrics .

metrics.name: Median days from submission to final decision
metrics.population: Manuscripts with a final accept/reject decision in 2025, including desk rejections; n not reported.
metrics.note: Population definition: https://academic.oup.com/pages/using-the-content/metrics .

metrics.name: Median days from acceptance to publication
metrics.population: Articles first published online in 2025; n not reported.
metrics.note: Population definition: https://academic.oup.com/pages/using-the-content/metrics .

metrics.name: Historical approximate acceptance proportion mentioned in 2020 editorial
metrics.population: Incoming journal papers; no rate period, cohort count or decision/submission denominator definition stated.
metrics.note: Editors' commentary published 20 August 2020. This does not establish an exact 2020 annual acceptance rate or a current rate.

audit_note: Access: page for current official author guidance, lower-case /about metric table and OUP definitions; upper-case /About initially timed out. Access: page for the 2020 primary editorial archived in PMC, retrieved in full via Python urllib after the web tool returned a browser challenge. Its text states about 20% acceptance without a rate period. European focus and relevant global-health contributions are fit conditions.

name: Annali dell'Istituto Superiore di Sanità
scope_notes: Italian national public-health institute journal with a broad health-science remit. Existing-data population studies and evidence synthesis fit when they contribute to public health. Regional or Italian data should be compared with European or international evidence; laboratory and clinical work elsewhere in its scope falls outside OSRI's initial program.

route.conditions: English-language submissions. Articles normally allow 6000 words and reviews 10000, with references included in those specified limits; supplementary material is limited to two printed pages. No paid excess-length option is stated. ISS-affiliated authors need internal authorization. Printed journal subscriptions are optional reader purchases. Apply the journal AI-use disclosure and permission requirements.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None for the standard author route; optional print subscriptions and any third-party permissions are separate.

fee_evidence.note: Full official policy expressly excludes article/submission processing charges and author publishing fees; separately lists optional reader print-subscription prices.
Full current author guidance establishes article/review and two-printed-page supplementary limits, ISS internal authorization and manuscript requirements; no compulsory author payment is stated.

difficulty.basis: The official process has editor screening and at least two reviewers, but no dated acceptance statistic or comparative contribution threshold was found. Comparing regional/Italian findings with European or international data is an explicit fit requirement, not automatic high difficulty.

metrics.name: Journal Impact Factor, publisher's year label
metrics.population: Journal-level citation metric; denominator and measurement window not stated in announcement.
metrics.note: Title/body explicitly say 2025; page metadata retains 2021-07-01. Preserve the publisher's label without treating the metadata date as the metric year; not acceptance evidence.

audit_note: Access: page for official About and impact-factor announcement. The announcement's old publication timestamp conflicts with its updated body; exact bibliometric window was not independently verified. No band was inferred from citation impact.

name: Epidemiologia e Serviços de Saúde: revista do SUS
publisher: Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde e Ambiente, Ministério da Saúde do Brasil
scope_notes: Population-health, epidemiology, management and policy evidence relevant to Brazil's Unified Health System (SUS). Existing-data analyses and systematic reviews fit; the Evidência em contexto category also accepts evidence synthesis, methods and policy interpretation. A concrete SUS contribution is required.

route.conditions: Portuguese manuscript and meaningful SUS contribution required. Submission, evaluation and publication are free; English full-text and Spanish-abstract translations are publisher-funded. Original articles, including systematic reviews, normally allow 3000 words; Evidência em contexto 2000. Meet data-availability and applicable ethics requirements and use a suitable free repository where deposit is required.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None for the stated journal route, including its provided translations; no compulsory author membership stated.

fee_evidence.note: Complete current official policy explicitly excludes submission/evaluation/publication fees under diamond access and states that English/Spanish translations are free, funded by the Brazilian Ministry of Health; author language and article limits are on the same page.

difficulty.basis: Current official policy describes scope assessment, methodological-quality screening and external scientific-merit review. No dated acceptance statistics or comparative selectivity threshold were found. Evidence relevant to Brazil's SUS is a scope requirement, not a difficulty ranking.

audit_note: Access: page for the complete current official SciELO journal policy in Portuguese. Its estimated 90-day editorial evaluation is a policy estimate, not a measured year-specific median or acceptance metric; it was not placed in metrics.

name: Journal of the College of Community Physicians of Sri Lanka
publisher: College of Community Physicians of Sri Lanka
scope_notes: Society journal covering epidemiology, demography, statistics, population health and health policy. Accepts local and international authors. Existing-data population studies and public-health reviews fit; manuscripts should address a contemporary public-health question.

route.conditions: English manuscripts from local or international authors; no college membership prerequisite is stated. Original research normally has a 3000-word limit and reviews 4500. Studies normally should be within five years; exceptions are assessed case by case. Authors must provide adequate English, but purchase of editing services is not required. No paid excess-page route is stated.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None for standard submission, processing and publication; no compulsory membership or editing service stated.

fee_evidence.note: Full current instructions expressly exclude submission/publication fees and separately processing/publishing fees. They welcome local/international authors and set length/recency requirements; English support is advisory, with no mandated purchase.

difficulty.basis: Review evaluates originality, scientific validity, ethics and public-health implications. Those criteria and two independent reviewers do not establish a comparative difficulty band. No dated official acceptance statistics were found; country/society identity does not imply easier acceptance.

audit_note: Access: page for full official editorial policies. A usual 2–6-week first-decision interval is an undated process expectation with no sample definition, not a measured annual performance statistic.

name: Delaware Journal of Public Health
publisher: Delaware Academy of Medicine / Delaware Public Health Association
scope_notes: Society journal emphasizing Delaware and surrounding states; national/international work is considered at editorial discretion. Existing population-data research, systematic reviews and policy analysis need a clear connection to its regional public-health readership and an appropriate themed issue.

route.conditions: Standard article submission, processing and publication are free. Select the relevant upcoming themed issue and deadline and show Delaware/regional public-health relevance. October 2025 instructions normally allow 7500 words for research, 4000 for systematic reviews/analytic essays; references/tables/figures are excluded from text totals. No paid excess-page option stated. Optional reprints/advertisements and sponsor-supported supplements are outside this route.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None for standard articles; no compulsory membership stated. Optional reprints, advertisements and supplement sponsorship are separate.

fee_evidence.note: Current full official page excludes submission/processing costs and explicitly all article submission/publication fees; author reprints and advertising are separate services.

Official author instructions revised 1 October 2025 repeat no submission costs and state article-type length limits. Supplement issues have external support; no compulsory author page/membership payment is stated.

difficulty.basis: Official peer-review guidance evaluates scientific/policy/analytic value and robustness. No dated acceptance statistics or comparative selectivity threshold were found. Delaware/regional relevance, the chosen issue theme and its deadline are fit conditions; regional publication does not imply easy acceptance.

audit_note: Access: page for complete official peer-review and submission pages. Submission expressly does not guarantee publication. No population-wide acceptance percentage inferred from output or submission instructions.

name: Preventing Chronic Disease
publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
scope_notes: Chronic-disease prevention and population-health practice, including surveillance/survey and GIS analyses, evaluation and systematic reviews. Scoping reviews are excluded from the systematic-review category. The methods label maps to practical instructional Tools for Public Health Practice articles, which require a one-paragraph summary to the editor before manuscript submission; it does not establish a generic algorithm-paper format. Current guidance says submitted data should be the most current and no older than two years.

route.conditions: Ordinary submission/publication has no journal fees under the blanket author-cost policy. Follow article-specific limits and the two-year data-recency policy. Tools for Public Health Practice requires an editor summary before submission and is an instructional methods format. CDC publication and reuse-permission policies apply. No paid membership or editing prerequisite is stated.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None for the ordinary author route. Costs of obtaining permission for chosen third-party material are external and author dependent.

fee_evidence.note: Independent full-page read confirms the blanket exclusion of publishing-related charges, separately free reader access, and current-data guidance. This is author-cost evidence rather than reader access alone.
Fee auditor directly inspected ordinary submission instructions and found no payment prerequisite; retained as the fee auditor's evidence, not a newly independent read in skeptical review.
Independent full-page read confirms peer-reviewed research/review formats and the prior editor-summary requirement for instructional Tools for Public Health Practice articles.

difficulty.basis: Provisional agent judgment: a CDC announcement explicitly reports 14.2% acceptance in 2025, while editorial policy prioritizes novel ideas for a broad public-health audience. The denominator and article mix are not disclosed. The two-year data recency requirement is a fit condition, not a prestige measure.

metrics.name: Reported acceptance rate
metrics.population: Journal manuscripts; exact submission/decision cohort definition, denominator count and article-type mix not disclosed.
metrics.note: Announcement explicitly assigns the rate to 2025; About-page Quick Stats alone does not give the rate year. Not manuscript-specific odds.

metrics.name: Journal Impact Factor
metrics.population: Journal-level citation metric; underlying citable-item count not disclosed in Quick Stats.
metrics.note: Official page labels 2025, reported in 2026. This is separate from acceptance difficulty.

audit_note: Independent review supports verified_free: the full general-author policy excludes all publishing-associated author fees, and no contradictory charge was found. No artificial separate-sentence submission-fee uncertainty is introduced. Corrected methods fit and its prior-summary condition. Independently read current editorial and article-type policies plus the official announcement at https://www.cdc.gov/PCD/announcements.htm ; the announcement explicitly assigns 14.2% acceptance and JIF 5.6 to 2025. Denominator/article mix remain unknown and high remains a provisional agent judgment. No venue contact was made.

name: Medical Care Research and Review
scope_notes: Fits existing-data analyses, syntheses and methodological brief reports about health-service organization, financing, delivery or related policy. Manuscripts need an explicit new contribution; theory/conceptual framing is important. Reviews follow PRISMA. Preprints are considered; supply the DOI, disclose them and do not update them during journal evaluation. Substantive GenAI use requires disclosure and output verification; the publisher prohibits specified content/data uses. Independent authors are eligible, subject to possible additional integrity documentation.

route.conditions: Standard subscription publication has no submission or publication fee. Optional Sage Choice open access and specifically requested print color cost extra; online color is free. Stay within article limits: empirical research 6,000 words, reviews 8,000, brief reports 2,500, excluding abstract, tables, figures and references.
route.other_mandatory_costs: No compulsory membership, registration, page or overlength payment is stated for manuscripts within the article limits; journal policy expressly excludes submission and publication fees.

fee_evidence.note: Journal-specific policy explicitly states that submission and publication carry no fees; distinguishes optional open access and print color costs.

difficulty.basis: New-contribution sections, conceptual framing and rigor are documented submission requirements. They do not establish relative selectivity within health-services research, and no defined acceptance cohort or comparative editorial evidence was verified. Agent judgment: unknown; no easy-acceptance implication.

audit_note: Read official article-type and contribution requirements. Sage journal metrics/overview endpoints were inaccessible or timed out, including an ordinary HTTPS attempt. No current dated citation value or acceptance cohort was verified; third-party figures were excluded. Skeptical review: Reopened the journal-specific fee, format and review policy; retained verified_free. Added applicable author-policy conditions. publisher: Wrocław University of Science and Technology, Faculty of Management
scope_notes: OR methodology and quantitative decision-making applications, with explicit coverage of optimization, forecasting, simulation, game theory and decision support. Existing-data economic, social and management applications fit.

route.conditions: Current author instructions explicitly exclude both APCs and submission charges; the homepage also excludes publication fees and the aims page describes an institution-funded free journal. No selective waiver or affiliation agreement is required. Non-survey manuscripts may have at most 35 references. Revised manuscripts must use the journal LaTeX template and EPS figures; converted Word source or converted raster figures are not accepted. No compulsory membership, registration payment or page tariff is stated.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None stated in the explicit no-APC/no-submission-charge policy and current author instructions; no compulsory membership, paid provider or conference registration is listed.

fee_evidence.note: The final policy paragraph explicitly excludes APCs and submission charges. The page also specifies the 35-reference limit for non-survey papers and the LaTeX/EPS revision requirements. Independently read through the web tool and confirmed in a separate live HTML request.
The official homepage explicitly identifies open access without a publication fee.
The university journal describes itself as free of charge and financed by the Faculty of Management, corroborating the author-instruction fee statement.

difficulty.basis: The official author instructions require substantial theoretical OR-methodology discussion or quantitative decision-making applications and permit current-topic reviews. The homepage displays 6.68% acceptance calculated since 01/01/2025, but does not give the end date, counts or denominator. Retain the official statistic with those limits; the incomplete interval and population prevent a comparative difficulty band.

metrics.name: Acceptance rate
metrics.population: Unknown: the source does not state the denominator, counts, or treatment of pending submissions and revisions.
metrics.note: The page labels its metrics as calculated since 01/01/2025. No end date or denominator is supplied; do not call this a 2025 annual rate or assume the access date closes the reporting period.

metrics.name: Journal Impact Factor
metrics.population: Journal citation metric; underlying citation and citable-item counts are not supplied on this page.
metrics.note: Official publisher-reported value. Citation impact is not an acceptance rate and does not determine the difficulty band.

metrics.name: CiteScore
metrics.population: Journal citation metric; underlying citation/document counts and calculation window are not supplied on this page.
metrics.note: The homepage explicitly labels this 2025 Cite Score and links to monthly Scopus updates. Transcribed as the journal reports it, without treating it as acceptance selectivity.

audit_note: Skeptical review corrects the earlier fee audit: the current author instructions expressly exclude submission charges as well as APCs. The prior needs_verification decision missed that final paragraph. Upgrade to verified_free on journal-specific evidence, preserving formatting constraints and leaving the incomplete acceptance-rate period and denominator unchanged.

name: ORiON
publisher: Operations Research Society of South Africa (ORSSA)
scope_notes: OR theory, methodological reviews, case studies and applications; explicit topics include queues, allocation, multicriteria decisions, optimization, reliability and computer simulation. Particularly oriented toward practitioners and problems in Southern Africa or comparable settings, so regional relevance must be explained.

route.conditions: Official policy explicitly excludes APCs and page fees under a Submission Fees heading; separate submission-fee wording remains unresolved. The submission checklist and guidelines state no membership or conference-registration payment and no manuscript page cap. Research articles have a distinct peer-review route; special issues require invitation.
route.other_mandatory_costs: Page fees explicitly absent; no required membership payment is stated. Separate submission-fee confirmation remains unresolved.

fee_evidence.note: The official journal page states that it charges neither APCs nor page fees, under a Submission Fees heading. This supports free publication but leaves the literal submission-fee wording incomplete.
Submission checklist and guidelines do not state a membership payment or other mandatory charge.

difficulty.basis: The official society-journal scope requires useful new theory, novel case-study approaches, demonstrable OR application success or useful methodological reviews, with research articles undergoing double-blind review. These criteria help assess fit and contribution but do not disclose comparative selectivity. No official citation or acceptance metric was located in the journal about/submission pages and targeted official-site search inspected.

audit_note: Retain needs_verification. The official Submission Fees section explicitly excludes APCs and page fees, but its sentence does not expressly exclude submission fees. Checked the submission checklist and author guidelines; no author membership, conference-registration payment or manuscript page cap is specified.

name: RAIRO - Operations Research
publisher: EDP Sciences, in partnership with SMAI and scientific participation of ROADEF
scope_notes: Pure and applied OR, including mathematical programming, graph algorithms, scheduling, logistics, decision support, and deterministic, stochastic and robust models. Society scope supports original theoretical, methodological, algorithmic and application studies.

route.conditions: Publisher-supported Subscribe to Open route confirmed for 2026 content. The publisher excludes submission fees and provides free publication for the mathematics S2O journals, including authors at institutions without an S2O subscription. No selective waiver is needed. Open-access status is decided annually; recheck the eventual publication year. Journal-specific length/production instructions remain unreadable because of HTTP 403.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None stated for mathematics S2O journals in the publisher free-publication policy; no author membership or institutional-subscription requirement.

fee_evidence.note: Publisher policy expressly excludes submission fees across its journals and lists RAIRO - Operations Research within the S2O programme.
The current FAQ identifies RAIRO in the mathematics programme and says authors publish in these mathematics journals open access free of charge; A&A page-charge exceptions are separately identified.
The publisher 11 June 2026 update confirms that RAIRO - Operations Research reached the threshold for open access publication of its 2026 content.
Publisher programme page identifies RAIRO and states that no-APC S2O applies even to submissions from institutions without an S2O subscription.
Journal-specific author instructions could not be read because the site returned HTTP 403.

difficulty.basis: The official associated-society page welcomes high-level original theoretical, methodological, algorithmic and applied OR contributions under international scientific standards. This supplies contribution criteria but no comparative selectivity statistic; journal home and aims pages returned HTTP 403 in this audit. The publisher citation metrics cannot establish acceptance difficulty.

metrics.name: Journal Impact Factor
metrics.population: Journal citation metric; underlying citation and citable-item counts are not supplied on this page.
metrics.note: Official publisher-reported value. Citation impact is not an acceptance rate and does not determine the difficulty band.

metrics.name: CiteScore
metrics.population: Journal citation metric; underlying citation/document counts are not supplied in the publisher news item.
metrics.note: Publisher announcement dated 2025-07-17 explicitly describes the 2024 Journal Citation Reports and CiteScores. The publication date is not the metric year; not acceptance selectivity.

audit_note: Retain verified_free for the confirmed 2026 S2O volume. Independently verified publisher no-submission-fee policy, journal inclusion, mathematics S2O free-publication policy and the 11 June 2026 confirmation. Membership and an author-institution subscription are not conditions. Journal-specific length/production instructions remain blocked by HTTP 403; recheck the publication year because S2O opening is decided annually.

name: Journal of Machine Learning Research
scope_notes: Machine learning theory, algorithms, analysis and methodological insight. Routine applications of ML to other domains are excluded. Unsolicited surveys are not considered; separate open-source-software guidance applies.

route.conditions: The standard journal publication has no publication fee. A submission-fee exclusion was not found in the author page or FAQ, so the combined zero-cost route remains unverified. LaTeX and the JMLR style are required. Over 35 pages can delay review; over 50 pages, including appendices, requires justification and can lead to desk rejection. These are editorial length conditions, not a documented paid overlength option. Unsolicited surveys are excluded.
route.other_mandatory_costs: Publication charges are excluded. Submission charges remain unknown; no compulsory paid membership or conference registration was identified in the inspected instructions.

fee_evidence.note: Explicitly excludes publication fees and documents length and preparation conditions, but does not explicitly exclude submission fees.
Describes account registration and submission workflow; does not provide an explicit submission-fee or blanket no-author-fee policy.

difficulty.basis: Agent judgment for the main ML research track: requires substantive advances in understanding with broader ML interest, rigorous support and substantial additions beyond a prior conference version. This is a contribution-threshold judgment, not a measured current acceptance probability; MLOSS software has separate criteria.

metrics.name: Median submission-to-first-review-decision time (days)
metrics.population: Papers sent to reviewers; desk rejections excluded
metrics.note: Historical 2021 median, reported 2022-02-21; not a current turnaround promise.

audit_note: The current statistics page presents submission and decision-time plots without an accessible numerical acceptance-rate table. The 2022 retrospective's historical 'current 17%' lacks an unambiguous cohort year in its text and was not imported as a current or dated-cohort rate.

name: Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research
scope_notes: AI methods, reasoning, knowledge representation, agents, NLP, planning, vision and learning. Research articles, analytical surveys and technical notes must advance understanding beyond a narrow application.

route.conditions: No submission or publication fees. The ordinary journal route needs no conference participation. Authors supply publication-ready files and the mandatory reproducibility checklist; surveys have separate contribution requirements. Long articles may take longer to review, without a paid length option in the inspected policy. AI may assist research, but core contributions must come from the human authors.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None for the ordinary journal route under the explicit free-submission/free-publication policy; no paid membership or required event registration is specified.

fee_evidence.note: Explicitly says authors are not charged for submitting or publishing articles.
Independently rules out submission and accepted-article publication fees; documents author preparation, checklist, survey and AI requirements.

difficulty.basis: Agent judgment within AI methods: the current transparency page reports strong overall modeled selection and screening for results important to the AI community, including methodological advances beyond a domain application. Its overall and post-screening probabilities refer to different populations; neither predicts the fate of an individual paper.

metrics.name: Modeled overall acceptance probability, possibly after one revision
metrics.population: Initial-submission model including summary rejection; underlying manuscript count not stated in accessible text
metrics.note: Data 2025-01-01 to 2026-01-01; released 2026-04-16. Model allows one revised resubmission after six weeks. Not a raw accepted/submitted rate.

metrics.name: Modeled acceptance probability conditional on no summary rejection
metrics.population: Model conditioned on submissions not summarily rejected; underlying manuscript count not stated in accessible text
metrics.note: Same period and release. Includes possible revised resubmission; do not apply to all initial submissions.

metrics.name: Modeled expected time to acceptance (weeks)
metrics.population: Acceptance-path model, possibly after one revision; not all submitted manuscripts
metrics.note: Same period and release; assumes six weeks to resubmit. Expected time, not a guarantee.

audit_note: Verified the official textual model and conditioning. Its linked process diagram returned HTTP 403, so raw branch counts, full branch calculations and sample denominators were not independently recovered. The page excludes the 90 days before release to reduce pending-submission distortion. No raw acceptance rate is asserted.

name: Transactions on Machine Learning Research
publisher: Transactions on Machine Learning Research (self-published; part of Journal of Machine Learning Research Inc.)
scope_notes: Original ML studies, methods, reproducibility and applications yielding insight into learning methods. Survey submissions are excluded from September 1, 2026, despite a Survey Certification still appearing in the editorial page. Archival conference-paper extensions are excluded; preprints and expressly non-archival workshop overlap can be eligible. Current official pages differ in specificity on LLM use: the editorial policy permits assistive tools, while the FAQ expects human-sourced ideas, claims and results and requires first-page disclosure.

route.conditions: No author fees. Every author needs an active OpenReview profile and sufficient annual submission quota, including for desk-rejected submissions. Length must be justified. No surveys from September 1, 2026; no expanded archival conference papers. The editorial LLM policy allows assistive use with human responsibility; the FAQ additionally expects human-sourced ideas/claims/results and first-page disclosure. Assess both against the actual workflow. Journal-to-conference presentation and attendance are separate.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None for journal submission and publication under the blanket no-author-fee policy. Journal-to-conference travel or registration is outside this route and is not required to publish.

fee_evidence.note: Blanket policy imposes no fees or payments on authors; annual quotas and originality rules govern eligibility.
Any manuscript length is permitted if justified; active author profiles and the required format are documented.
Excludes surveys from September 1, 2026; distinguishes conference presentation opportunities and states human-contribution and LLM-disclosure expectations.

difficulty.basis: Agent judgment within ML research, based on an explicitly less significance-selective acceptance model: accurate convincing evidence, clear communication and findings of interest to some ML researchers. Method novelty, state-of-the-art results, significance and impact are not necessary acceptance gates. Technical rigor remains necessary; this band gives no numerical odds.

audit_note: No official numerical acceptance-rate series was located in inspected policy/FAQ pages. OpenReview public papers exclude desk rejections, so counting visible accepted/rejected papers would miss part of the submission population. Independent review confirmed the no-fee policy and current acceptance criteria. Retain the FAQ survey exclusion over the residual certification description; do not interpret the broader editorial LLM wording as cancelling the FAQ conditions. Sources: https://jmlr.org/tmlr/editorial-policies.html ; https://jmlr.org/tmlr/faq.html .

name: Journal of Open Source Software
scope_notes: Peer-reviewed papers about mature research software; requires more than six months of active public development and demonstrated research use, which may be by the developers. External community adoption is a positive signal, not mandatory. Pre-trained models, notebooks, thin API clients and one-off tools are outside scope. Humans must make core design decisions and validate AI-assisted work.

route.conditions: No fees to submit or publish. Requires mature, research-used software under an OSI-approved license, tests, documentation and more than six months of active public development. A major contributor submits, participates in public review and archives a tagged release with a DOI. AI assistance requires disclosure and human validation; AI-mediated author/editor or reviewer conversation is prohibited except translation. Models, notebooks, thin API clients and one-off analysis tools are outside scope.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None in the journal submission/publication policy. Repository hosting must permit free public access; free supported archive choices exist. Existing software development expenses are not journal charges.

fee_evidence.note: Explicitly excludes submission and publication fees and documents public-development maturity, research impact, AI limits, open hosting, public review and archived-release requirements.

difficulty.basis: Agent judgment withheld for relative editorial selectivity. Software must show research use, substantial design contribution, tests/documentation and more than six months of active public development. These are substantial maturity and preparation gates; their effort does not establish research-journal prestige or acceptance probability.

audit_note: Independent review confirmed current maturity, research-use and AI conditions. The existing route correctly prohibits AI-mediated author/editor/reviewer conversation except translation. Old stage-rejection estimates lack precise periods/denominators and predate current criteria; they remain excluded. Source: https://joss.readthedocs.io/en/latest/submitting.html .

name: Journal of Statistical Software
scope_notes: Substantial open-source statistical software and reproducible articles, including smaller code snippets. Methods innovations should be published elsewhere first; a JSS implementation needs its own substantial software contribution.

route.conditions: Free submission and no author fees. Requires GPL or GPL-compatible software, manuscript source and replication material reproducing all results. Authors prepare final publishable files. No page, figure or table limit applies; manuscripts over 30 pages can take longer to review. The journal does not supply paid conversion assistance as a prerequisite.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None under the journal-wide no-author-fee policy; no compulsory paid membership, event registration or page charges are specified.

fee_evidence.note: States free-submission publishing and no author fees; specifies software licensing, reproducibility, author typesetting and no page/figure/table limits.

difficulty.basis: Skeptical-review judgment: substantial statistical-software contribution, comparative discussion and exact reproducibility are explicit requirements. Regular articles and narrower code snippets have different contribution scopes. These requirements establish preparation and scientific standards, but the inspected official pages do not calibrate a comparative high acceptance-difficulty band. Unknown does not imply easy acceptance.

audit_note: No official acceptance-rate or dated numerical citation-metric series was located on inspected mission, author, home and about pages. Code snippets have a narrower contribution scope than regular articles. Independent review retained the explicit free-submission/no-author-fee route and software/manuscript peer review, but changed high to unknown: implementation scope and reproducibility burden do not alone establish comparative selectivity.

name: Logical Methods in Computer Science
publisher: Logical Methods in Computer Science e.V.
scope_notes: Original logic-related theoretical/practical computer-science research and surveys. The required pre-review arXiv/CoRR deposit includes cs.LO and TeX sources. The arXiv CS rule requiring prior successful journal/conference peer review for surveys creates an unresolved prerequisite conflict for a new LMCS survey. Verify a permitted deposit/submission arrangement before treating an unpublished survey as eligible; no exception was established here.

route.conditions: Free Episciences overlay-journal route. First post the paper and TeX source in arXiv/CoRR with cs.LO included, then submit through Episciences. Normally at most 50 pages; justify longer papers to the handling editor. Repository endorsement and moderation apply separately. Survey authors must check the arXiv CS prior-peer-review prerequisite before assuming the required deposit is available.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None under the applicable Episciences no-payment model; no paid membership or conference registration is required by the ordinary journal workflow.

fee_evidence.note: Applies to all Episciences journals: no publication or access fees; submission and publication are not conditional on a per-unit fee.
Establishes LMCS as the free overlay journal and gives its arXiv/CoRR, TeX-source and 50-page conditions.
arXiv CS surveys and position papers require documented successful prior journal/conference peer review; this can constrain the prerequisite deposit for LMCS surveys.

difficulty.basis: Agent judgment withheld: original logic-related research/surveys undergo two or three referees, but generic highest-quality language and review procedure do not establish a calibrated comparative selectivity band. The stronger special policy for long-standing open-problem claims is not generalized to all submissions. Unknown does not mean easier.

audit_note: No official dated acceptance-rate or citation-metric series was found in the inspected author, policy, purpose and home pages. Independent review confirmed the current deposit workflow and platform no-payment policy. The survey-deposit conflict is a reviewer inference from two official policies, not an announced LMCS ban or established exception. Sources: https://lmcs.episciences.org/page/authors-information ; https://www.episciences.org/publishing-model/ ; https://blog.arxiv.org/2025/10/31/attention-authors-updated-practice-for-review-articles-and-position-papers-in-arxiv-cs-category/ .

name: Journal of Object Technology
publisher: Association Internationale pour les Technologies Objets (AITO)
scope_notes: Software and language engineering, model-driven engineering, architecture, verification, maintenance, analytics, and software tools. Generic domain applications without a software-engineering contribution are outside scope.

route.conditions: All journal contributions are completely free for authors and readers, without APCs. This audit covers the ordinary journal route; conference-linked issues may have separate event conditions. JOT LaTeX is mandatory. No fixed page limit; typical papers are 25–30 pages and longer work needs justification. Software Section papers require a usable binary, examples and an issue tracker, plus an established user community or previously peer-reviewed underpinning technology.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None under the blanket free-to-authors policy for ordinary journal publication; no paid AITO membership or required conference registration appears in that route.

fee_evidence.note: States completely free access for authors and readers, applicable to all contributions, and no APCs.
Documents the ordinary submission workflow, required LaTeX template and absence of a fixed page limit.
Documents Software Section maturity and artifact requirements; does not turn them into a publication fee.

difficulty.basis: Agent judgment withheld for relative selectivity across research articles, surveys, mature practice reports and software. Originality, significance, soundness and presentation are assessed; conference extensions require at least 30% new material. These rules identify contribution gates without supplying comparable current acceptance odds.

audit_note: A 2010 farewell editorial reports about 30% acceptance without a defined observation window or counts; this old, underspecified figure was excluded. Event-specific editorial acceptance rates are not the ordinary journal rate. Source inspected: https://www.jot.fm/issues/issue_2010_05/editorial.pdf . Independent review confirmed the blanket free-to-authors policy, current submission scope and Software Section peer-review/artifact requirements. The legacy authors.html page timed out in this review; accessible current software and submission-system pages were added as corroborating evidence.

name: Transactions on Graph Data and Knowledge
scope_notes: Graph algorithms and databases, knowledge graphs, graph representation learning, semantic web, querying, reasoning and related data-science methods. Publishes research, resource and survey articles; resources may include data or software.

route.conditions: No fees for authors or readers, supported by SWSA. Ordinary journal submission requires no society membership or event participation. Research and resource articles need a Supplementary Material Statement even when no relevant resources exist, ORCIDs and the journal template. Resource submissions have no fixed upper/lower page limit, with 10–20 pages expected. Substantive GenAI use must be declared and humans remain responsible.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None under the journal-specific no-author-fee policy; SWSA support is not an author membership charge. No paid page or registration requirement is imposed on the ordinary journal route.

fee_evidence.note: Aims and Processing Charge sections explicitly exclude all author/reader fees. Submission, Resource Articles and GenAI sections establish the stated nonmonetary conditions.

difficulty.basis: Skeptical-review judgment: research, survey and resource submissions have distinct novelty, impact and quality criteria. These are documented contribution requirements, but the inspected policy does not establish comparative acceptance difficulty for the combined venue. No measured odds or calibrated high band is inferred from generic state-of-the-art and peer-review requirements.

audit_note: Inspected review process, calls and resource criteria. No dated acceptance-rate series was located. Special-issue guidance explicitly avoids enforcing a fixed acceptance rate; three-review procedure and the two-strike revision rule are process constraints, not measured selectivity. Independent review retained journal-specific no-author-fee evidence, peer review and three article types; replaced high with unknown because the documented criteria do not establish a calibrated comparative band.

name: Journal of Data Mining and Digital Humanities
publisher: CNRS, INRAE and INRIA joint journal project; Episciences platform
scope_notes: Computational research on human-produced humanities and social data, including text mining, NLP, information retrieval, data quality, visualization, corpora and reproducible data analysis. Also accepts peer-reviewed short papers describing useful tools, datasets and community resources.

route.conditions: No submission or publication fee. Deposit a preprint in HAL, arXiv or Zenodo and submit its repository identifier through Episciences. Accepted files use the journal toolkit; English and reproducible work are expected. Short tool, dataset and community-resource papers receive peer review. The inspected instructions specify no paid overlength option. Conference listings do not make attendance a prerequisite for the ordinary journal route.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None under the explicit no-author-fee policy; no paid membership or required conference registration is specified for ordinary journal submission.

fee_evidence.note: Cost section explicitly excludes submission, publication and all author fees; short papers/community reports are peer reviewed.
Requires supported repository deposit, an account and the repository ID; final formatting follows acceptance.

difficulty.basis: Agent judgment withheld: the official policy specifies at least two editor-reviewers, iterative correction and agreement before acceptance, including peer-reviewed short software/dataset/community reports. It does not supply a discriminating editorial-selectivity threshold or measured acceptance odds.

audit_note: No official dated acceptance or citation metrics located in inspected pages. Review deadlines on the policy page describe intended process, not observed performance.

name: Australasian Journal of Information Systems
publisher: Australasian Chapter of the Association for Information Systems (AAIS)
scope_notes: Global information-systems theory/practice and conceptual development, with particular interest in Australasia. Ordinary Research Articles receive double-blind peer review. A submission must not already be available on a preprint service, so public-preprint-first workflows conflict with its checklist. Institutional credentials may be replaced by an explanation; this is not the same as an absolute institutional-affiliation requirement. Several named sections are closed and ACIS selected papers require invitation.

route.conditions: No submission fees, APCs, access fees or other charges. Use the ordinary Research Articles route; several named sections are closed and ACIS selected papers require invitation. Manuscripts must not already be on a preprint service. Use institutional credentials or explain their absence, supply data assurance, disclose substantive AI use and agree to review later submissions. Expected length is 20–30 A4 pages; substantial departures need editorial justification.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None: the journal excludes any other fees or charges. The future-reviewer commitment is a nonmonetary obligation, not a paid membership. Ordinary Research Articles do not require ACIS registration.

fee_evidence.note: Explicitly excludes submission fees, APCs and every other form of fees or charges.
Documents preprint prohibition, credential explanation, data assurance, AI disclosure, reviewer commitment, length guidance, open Research Articles and closed/restricted sections.

difficulty.basis: Skeptical-review judgment: relevance, contribution, originality, impact, conceptual soundness and appropriate methods are stated assessment criteria, applied differently by article type. They establish scholarly expectations but no comparative selectivity threshold or observed acceptance series. Undated A-list claims and short workflow targets are not acceptance odds.

audit_note: No official numerical acceptance series was located. Undated A-list claims were not converted to dated metrics or acceptance odds. Published workflow targets are not observed turnaround statistics. Independent review retained explicit zero submission/APC/other fees and verified the preprint prohibition. Changed high to unknown because general assessment criteria and undated rankings do not calibrate comparative difficulty.

name: e-Informatica Software Engineering Journal
publisher: Wrocław University of Science and Technology
scope_notes: Empirical software engineering, including AI/ML, tools, methods and systematic reviews with a direct software-engineering contribution. Mandatory author metadata includes affiliation-related email and public ORCID name plus university/company affiliation; unaffiliated-author exceptions remain unverified. Generative AI in manuscript writing is restricted to language/readability improvement, distinct from AI research methods.

route.conditions: No journal fees or paper-length limit. Must-have requirements specify affiliation-related email and public ORCID name plus university/company affiliation for all authors; no unaffiliated-author exception was established. Revised/final manuscripts require journal LaTeX; declarations and a hand-signed agreement are required. Generative AI in writing is restricted to language/readability improvement with disclosure and human responsibility. verified_free describes the monetary route for eligible authors, not universal author or workflow eligibility.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None under the homepage's journal-wide no-fees statement; no paid membership, conference registration or overlength surcharge is specified.

fee_evidence.note: Official current homepage states open access without any fees, no paper-length limit and university support.
Author FAQ independently gives a publication fee of zero dollars.
Documents required declarations, LaTeX revision files and the restrictive generative-AI writing policy.

difficulty.basis: Agent judgment withheld for comparative selectivity: requires substantial original contribution directly to software engineering and assessment of originality, innovation and analytical/theoretical strength by at least two reviewers. Its citation metrics describe citation performance, not ease of acceptance.

metrics.name: Journal Impact Factor
metrics.population: Citation metric for the journal; source gives no underlying citation/item counts
metrics.note: Official journal-reported 2025 metric. Citation performance only; provider calculation not independently audited.

metrics.name: Five-year Journal Impact Factor
metrics.population: Five-year citation metric for the journal; source gives no underlying counts
metrics.note: Official journal-reported 2025 metric; not editorial selectivity.

metrics.name: Scopus CiteScore
metrics.population: Scopus journal citation metric; source gives no underlying citation/document counts
metrics.note: Official journal-reported 2025 value with Scopus link; not acceptance probability.

metrics.name: Source Normalized Impact per Paper (SNIP)
metrics.population: Field-normalized journal citation metric; source gives no underlying counts
metrics.note: Official journal-reported 2025 value; not acceptance probability.

audit_note: Independent review confirmed journal-wide no fees and journal-reported 2025 citation metrics. Mandatory affiliation metadata has no located unaffiliated-author exception. Sources: https://www.e-informatyka.pl/ ; https://www.e-informatyka.pl/einformatica/authors-guide/paper-requirements-and-recommendations/ .

name: Journal of Graph Algorithms and Applications
publisher: Journal of Graph Algorithms and Applications; electronic edition hosted by Brown University Department of Computer Science
scope_notes: Design, analysis, implementation and applications of graph algorithms; includes network analysis, graph drawing, database and knowledge-representation algorithms, software engineering and biomedical-informatics applications when graph-algorithm research is central. Regular, concise and survey papers are eligible.

route.conditions: Diamond journal with no author charges. Requires LaTeX, numbered pages and lines, and journal-class final sources. Concise papers normally span 5–10 pages; the inspected regular-paper instructions do not specify a paid overlength option. Declare all generative AI use in submission comments; humans must validate its output and unattributed AI creation of scientific content is forbidden. Ordinary submission requires no conference attendance.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None under the journal-wide no-author-fee policy; no mandatory membership, registration or page charge is specified for ordinary journal articles.

fee_evidence.note: Identifies JGAA as diamond open access with no author fees; the open-access policy excludes author and reader charges.
Documents regular/concise/survey formats, 5–10-page concise papers, required preparation and AI disclosure/integrity requirements.

difficulty.basis: Agent judgment within graph-algorithms research: the journal explicitly selects a limited set of papers and says new/correct results alone are insufficient; work needs sufficient weight, interest and potential to stimulate further research. Preliminary screening can reject marginal-interest or insufficiently original papers. This supports a significance-selective band without numerical odds.

audit_note: No official dated acceptance-rate or citation-metric series found in inspected about/submission pages. Reviewer deadlines and review-time targets were not mistaken for observed medians.

name: Theory of Computing
publisher: Theory of Computing (community-run journal; main server provided by the University of Chicago Department of Computer Science)
scope_notes: Theoretical computer science research. Suitable for substantive mathematical and algorithmic contributions rather than routine informatics applications. The separate Graduate Surveys series is not treated as an unrestricted review-article route in this record.

route.conditions: No author fees. Post a LaTeX manuscript to arXiv under CC BY before submitting its identifier and cover letter through Episciences; authors format accepted papers in ToCTeX. The cover letter reports length, with no page-fee schedule in these instructions. Special handling applies to claimed solutions of long-standing complexity problems. arXiv endorsement and moderation remain separate from journal peer review.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None under the submission page's blanket no-author-fees policy; no paid membership or required conference registration is imposed by the ordinary journal workflow.

fee_evidence.note: No Author Fees section states free access for authors and readers; page updated March 3, 2026 documents repository submission and author final typesetting.

difficulty.basis: Agent judgment withheld: the current introduction establishes rigorous single-blind review and an aspiration to highest scientific quality, but it does not expose sufficiently specific comparative contribution thresholds or current selectivity statistics. Editorial-board reputation and indexing are not acceptance probabilities.

audit_note: No official numerical acceptance-rate or dated citation metrics located in inspected introductory/submission pages or bounded official-site search. The special policy for long-standing complexity claims is not a measure of all-paper selectivity.

name: Discrete Mathematics & Theoretical Computer Science
publisher: Discrete Mathematics & Theoretical Computer Science (Episciences overlay journal)
scope_notes: Original research at the intersection of discrete mathematics and theoretical computer science. Self-contained short notes are welcome; mathematical correctness, complete proofs and importance beyond the immediate referees are expected. Does not function as a preprint server.

route.conditions: No author or reader fees. Authors submit directly after depositing in HAL or arXiv and creating a platform account. Ordinary journal articles have no page restriction; accepted sources must use the journal LaTeX style. Generative AI use must be disclosed at submission. This audit excludes conference-proceedings participation or registration conditions.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None under the current journal-wide no-author-fee policy for regular articles; conference-associated routes require a separate event-cost audit.

fee_evidence.note: Author instructions updated October 1, 2026 exclude author/reader fees and document repository deposit, no regular-article page limit, final LaTeX and AI disclosure.
